scope: Linux x64 initial full-compiler loader optimization. Original Wasm, worker counts, host modules, SDK and test sources remain unchanged. Not complete runtime conformance or a stock cross-platform Bun result.
findings: Startup required 13985 individual WebAssembly.Table.grow calls per main/worker. Instrumented Bun workers spent 49-60 seconds inside those calls.
Reserve exactly the unique missing initial-main function slots in one growth. Existing freed slots retain priority, aliases share pointers, and later side-module behavior is unchanged.
A bulk-growth RangeError falls back to the original incremental allocation path; no extra capacity is reserved.

The uninstrumented ordinary console comparison went from 70.09 seconds on v98 Bun to 4.77 seconds on v104. The startup smoke finished in 4.42 seconds. Timings are individual executions, not statistical benchmarks.

All 16 targeted Node and Deno upstream registrations pass. Bun passes 15 and fails externBoxing because its filesystem realpath resolves the module root incorrectly. The identical source and invocation reproduce that failure on old v98 Bun and new v104 Bun; both Node versions and Deno match native Lean.

The initial native-table64 derivation stopped before executing any compiler because the transform accepted grow(1) but not grow(1n). That preparation failure is retained. Final controls cover both table widths.
remainingGaps: The Bun realPath discrepancy needs a separate repair and rerun.
Original Bun server cancellation deadlines need retesting with the faster startup.
Bun retains its Linux stack helper and lowered-memory workaround.
Full upstream suites, package integration and non-Linux validation remain unfinished; no remaining difference is established fundamental.
